main_text.p: 39. Rationalis est anima, qua homo non modò vivit, ac sentit, sed etiam intelligit, ratiocinatur, meminit, & e-ligit liberè: quæ quidem posteriora huic adsunt propria.

40. Obiectum eius, est omnis rerum species, tum sensu perceptibilis, tum eum quoq; fugiens. Per se verò nullum corporeum instrumentum ei tribuo; quòd etiam cùm se-parata fuerit à corpore hæc Anima, vires suas illa exsere-re possit. Interim tamen non iverim inficias, animalem virtutem in nobis multum conferre ad anima nostra, cor-pus etiamnum incolentis proprias operationes edendas.
Μόνῳ σοφῷ Θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἡ δόξα εἰς τὰς[?] αἰῶνας, אמן.

page.notes: No page number, catchword or signature is printed. The Greek line is a closing doxology; its final word is printed in Hebrew letters (אמן). The Greek accents and breathings are copied as far as legible, and τὰς is uncertain. The ornament and fleuron border carry no text. Some letters in the italic text are slightly blurred but readable.
